acceptanceCriteria: A local command (dogfood status or a pre-push hook usable by lanes) reports UNBOUND_COMMITS naming each commit after the last seal on the branch, exit non-zero
ci:batched PRs still run the unbound-commit scan (cheap, no race shards) so the failure is visible on the constituent PR
A fixture test covers a branch with a post-seal commit (refused) and a rebound branch (accepted); docs/DOGFOOD.md names the recovery
body: Observed 2026-10-18: PR #1113 (V1-1763) head 27fde1679 'fix Codex review findings' was committed and pushed after the branch's dogfood seal and never bound. The lane reported success; the PR CI was skipped (ci:batched). The defect surfaced only when batch PR #1120's dogfood-batch-check attempt 1 failed `unbound-commits count=1 27fde1679`, and the batch integrator had to bind it in a helper clone. Expected: a lane cannot hand back or push a branch with commits after the last seal without a local refusal naming them (e.g. a dogfood status/pre-push check, or a ci:batched PR check that runs the cheap unbound-commit scan of dogfood-batch-check on the PR head). Actual: no check runs until a batch is assembled.
title: Nothing refuses pushing a lane branch whose tip commit was made after the dogfood seal; only the batch-check of a later batch PR catches it
